base_member_text: [L2-L3,L56-L58,L84-L86,L90-L91,L95,L98] (MED/unchecked-mpi-status) Every MPI call overwrites ier without checking it, so communicator, datatype-construction, collective, or cleanup failures can be silently followed by further MPI operations.
audit_member_text: [L2-L3,L56-L58,L84-L91,L94-L98] (MED/unchecked MPI failures) MPI return codes are overwritten without inspection, allowing communicator, datatype, collective, or free errors to cascade through invalid handles and incomplete data.

adversarial.rationale: The missing local IERROR tests do not establish the claimed silent cascade: xmpi.F90:210-245 installs comm_errhandler on MPI_COMM_WORLD before splitting the compute communicator, and no returning error-handler configuration was found. That handler reports the error and calls halt_program, which reaches xmpi_abort and STOP (xmpi.F90:314-320,1680-1704); datatype operations likewise have fatal default handling rather than a configured return-and-continue path.

neutralizer.quote:
call MPI_Comm_get_name(comm,o,r,ier)
   call MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD,ra,ier)
   write(0,*) 'MPI process #',ra,'in ',o(1:r),' generated an error:',error_code
   call MPI_Error_string(error_code,e,r,ier)
   write(0,*) e(1:r)
   call halt_program

base_member_text: [L40-L55,L68-L83] (MED/unchecked-subarray-bounds) Subarray sizes and starts are derived from decomposition and border values without validating positivity or containment in shape(a)/shape(b), so small or inconsistent partitions can produce invalid MPI datatypes.
audit_member_text: [L39-L56,L67-L85] (MED/unchecked subarray bounds) Subtracting `2*nbord` can produce zero or negative subsizes, and adjusted starts and extents are never checked against `shape(a)` or `shape(b)` before datatype creation.

base_member_text: [L5-L8] (MED/communicator-mismatch) A root error detected for the supplied comm communicator aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD instead of comm, unexpectedly terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator.
audit_member_text: [L5-L8] (LOW/overbroad abort scope) A bad root for the supplied communicator aborts `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rather than `comm`, terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator invocation.

adversarial.rationale: Every in-tree matrix_coll caller in spaceparams.F90:833-1046 supplies xmpi_omaster and xmpi_ocomm; xmpi.F90:229-236 initializes these to MPI_COMM_WORLD and zero, with no later reassignment found. Thus the root-error branch is unreachable through these callers, and their communicator has no outside ranks for the claimed overbroad abort to affect.

neutralizer.quote:
xmpi_ocomm = MPI_COMM_WORLD
      call MPI_Comm_rank(xmpi_ocomm,xmpi_orank,ierr)
      call MPI_Comm_size(xmpi_ocomm,xmpi_osize,ierr)
      if (xmpi_osize < 2) then
         print *,'Number of MPI processes must be 2 or greater, but is:',xmpi_osize
         call halt_program(.false.)
      endif
      xmpi_omaster = 0

base_member_text: [L10-L15,L93-L100] (MED/allocation-lifetime) Six work arrays are allocated on every invocation but the template frees only MPI datatype handles and never deallocates the arrays.
[L6] (LOW/misleading-diagnostic) The hard-coded error text names matrix_distr_real8 even though this generic template does not establish that routine or type.

audit_member_text: [L38-L55,L65-L83] (HIGH/rank-to-decomposition off-by-one) For source rank `i-1` the root uses decomposition entry `i-1`, and rank `ra` sends dimensions from entry `ra`; this conflicts with the shard's distribution template mapping rank `r` to entry `r+1`, so gathered blocks can use the preceding rank's extents, offsets, and boundary flags.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The neutralizer is the separate I/O communicator: collection uses xmpi_ocomm (spaceparams.F90:974-976), whose rank 0 is excluded from the compute communicator and whose non-root rank ra maps to compute rank ra-1 (xmpi.F90:236-247,288-304). Decomposition entry compute_rank+1 therefore equals ra (spaceparams.F90:578-580), so collection entries ra and i-1 are correct; distribution uses the compute communicator (templates/space_distribute.mako:4-5), making its rank+1 indexing consistent rather than conflicting.
